question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ for the variables $x,y,z$ in that order.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form. Select the resulting augmented matrix.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right]
$$

metadata.domain: x,y,z real; p,q,s nonzero; nonsingular 3-by-3 coefficient matrix

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y-z &=-2 \\ x+2y &=-4 \\ -x-y &=5\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system. Select the solution $(x,y,z)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & -2 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & -4 \\ -1 & -1 & 0 & 5\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(-1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & -1 & 0 & 5\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=-2 \\ y &=3-(-1)(-2) \\ &=1 \\ x &=-2-(2)(1) \\ &\quad -(-1)(-2) \\ &=-6\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(-6,1,-2\right)
$$

metadata.domain: x,y,z real; p,q,s nonzero; nonsingular 3-by-3 coefficient matrix

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y-z &=-2 \\ -x-y+2z &=4 \\ -x+z &=3\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system. Select the solution $(x,y,z)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -1 & -2 \\ -1 & -1 & 2 & 4 \\ -1 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ -1 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=2 \\ y &=1-(0)(2) \\ &=1 \\ x &=-2-(1)(1) \\ &\quad -(-1)(2) \\ &=-1\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(-1,1,2\right)
$$
